extracted.intended_audience: beginner German learners / international students learning pronunciation and orthography
extracted.subtask_description: A beginner-focused pronunciation and usage guide for the three German umlaut vowels (ä, ö, ü), including how to say them (short/long), grammatical roles, typing methods, and alternative spellings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of umlauts
rubrics_metrics.description: Umlauts are diacritical marks represented by two dots (¨) placed above three vowels of the German alphabet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The German umlauts are ä, ö, and ü. They indicate vowel sound changes and distinguish between different words, verb forms, or grammatical features. Historically an “e” was added after the vowel (ae/oe/ue), which evolved into the two-dot mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: The three core umlaut letters
rubrics_metrics.description: The German alphabet includes three umlauts: Ä, Ö, and Ü (in addition to 26 letters and the ligature ß).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each umlaut is important for both grammar and pronunciation; presence or absence of an umlaut can completely change a word's meaning or function. The page lists example words: Ä – Äpfel, Ö – Österreich, Ü – Grüße.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short vs long umlaut distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Each umlaut (ä, ö, ü) is pronounced in two ways: short and long.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short umlauts are said quickly; long umlauts are held longer (often the same sound but lengthened, sometimes indicated historically by adding a silent 'h'). The page provides IPA symbols for short and long variants and audio examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronunciation guidance for Ä (short and long)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to pronounce Ä: Start with the English 'e' as in 'bed', keep mouth slightly more open, relax lips, tongue central; long Ä is the same sound lengthened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPA: Short Ä /ɛ/ (like 'e' in bed/bed/bet), Long Ä /ɛ:/ (start with short Ä and lengthen + add a silent H). Examples: Short Ä – Äpfel, Männer, Käse, März. Long Ä – Ähnlich, Mädchen, Nächste, Krähe. Note exception: when paired with 'u' (e.g., Läufer, Träume, Häufig) pronounce similar to 'oi' in 'ointment'. Audio recordings linked for short/long Ä.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronunciation guidance for Ö (short and long)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to pronounce Ö: purse the lips into a halfway circle (like 'O') and produce a sound similar to short Ä while holding that lip shape; long Ö is the lengthened version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPA: Short Ö [œ], Long Ö [ø]. English approximations: short Ö similar to French 'œ' in 'œuf' or 'u' in 'turn' (examples given like 'i' in flirt, 'o' in word); examples: Öffnen, Stöcke, Wörter, Löffel (short); Öl, Mögen, Böse, Hören (long). Audio recordings linked for short/long Ö.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronunciation guidance for Ü (short and long)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to pronounce Ü: begin with the 'ee' sound (as in 'see'), then purse the lips almost closed (as if whistling) while keeping the tongue position; long Ü is the lengthened version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPA: Short Ü [ʏ], Long Ü [yː]. Closest non-German examples are French 'u' in 'tu' or 'ue' in 'rue'. Examples: short – Rücken, Küche, Hütte, Müll; long – Bühne, Bücher, Üben, Mühle. Audio recordings linked for short/long Ü.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mouth-shape and articulatory tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete step-by-step mouth/tongue/lip instructions to produce each umlaut sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ä: slightly more open mouth than English 'e', tongue mid. Ö: purse lips into an O while producing a fronted vowel. Ü: say 'ee' and purse lips nearly shut. The guide emphasizes practicing visualization and provides a video for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: ä + u combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: When 'ä' is paired with the vowel 'u', pronunciation deviates from the usual Ä sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In combinations like 'Läufer', 'Träume', and 'Häufig', pronounce it similar to the 'oi' sound in the English word 'ointment'. The page flags this as an exception to normal Ä pronunciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function: umlauts indicate vowel sound changes and grammatical distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Umlauts serve to change vowel quality and mark grammatical differences (meaning, verb forms, number, mood, comparatives, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not using umlauts can confuse readers/listeners. The page lists specific grammatical patterns where umlauts appear (plurals, verb conjugations, subjunctive II, comparatives/superlatives, diminutives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage pattern: plural formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Many singular nouns form their plural by changing a vowel into an umlaut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: der Mann → die Männer; der Apfel → die Äpfel; der Vogel → die Vögel; das Wort → die Wörter; der Fuß → die Füße; der Kuss → die Küsse. The page shows a singular/plural table illustrating this pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage pattern: 2nd/3rd-person singular conjugation of strong verbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Some German strong (irregular) verbs change their stem vowel to an umlaut in the du/er/sie/es present-tense forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: backen — backe / bäckst / bäckt; fangen — fange / fängst / fängt; schlafen — schlafe / schläfst / schläft; waschen — wasche / wäschst / wäscht. The guide uses tables to show conjugation patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage pattern: Subjunctive II (Konjunktiv II)
rubrics_metrics.description: In many irregular verbs, the simple past stem vowel (a, o, u) becomes an umlaut in the Subjunctive II forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative examples: geben → gäbe; finden ich fand → ich fände; haben ich hatte → ich hätte; nehmen ich nahm → ich nähme; lesen ich las → ich läse; sein ich war → ich wäre. The page explains this helps differentiate subjunctive forms from indicative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage pattern: comparative and superlative adjectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Some adjectives form comparatives/superlatives by umlauting the stem vowel (a, o, u → ä, ö, ü) and adding comparative/superlative endings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: kalt → kälter → am kältesten; groß → größer → am größten; other examples: lang → länger, stark → stärker, alt → älter, jung → jünger. The guide provides example sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage pattern: diminutives causing umlaut changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When forming diminutives (using -chen or -lein), vowels a, o, u sometimes transform into umlauts; diminutives take the neuter article 'das'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: der Mann → das Männlein; der Baum → das Bäumchen; der Hund → das Hündchen; das Brot → das Brötchen. Bonus grammar note: all diminutives use 'das' regardless of original gender.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to type umlauts on Windows (ALT codes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Windows users can type umlauts using numeric ALT key combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed ALT codes: ä = ALT 0228, Ä = ALT 0196, ö = ALT 0246, Ö = ALT 0214, ü = ALT 0252, Ü = ALT 0220. The page presents a small table of lowercase/uppercase codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to type umlauts on macOS
rubrics_metrics.description: macOS users can type umlauts using Option+U then the letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortcut: Option + U, then release and type A/O/U to get Ä/Ö/Ü. The page lists this as the recommended macOS method.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to type umlauts on iOS (iPhone/iPad)
rubrics_metrics.description: On iOS, press-and-hold the base letter to pick accented variations or add a German keyboard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press and hold A/O/U then slide to select the umlauted variant; or add German keyboard via Settings > General > Keyboard > Keyboards > Add New Keyboard > German, then switch via globe icon.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to type umlauts on Android
rubrics_metrics.description: On Android, press-and-hold the base letter to access accented variants or add a German keyboard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press and hold A/O/U and slide to the umlaut variant; or add German keyboard via Settings > System > Language & input > Virtual keyboard > select keyboard > Languages > Add keyboard > German. Switch keyboards using the keyboard icon or long-press spacebar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative orthography using 'e' (ae/oe/ue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Umlauts can be written as two-letter combinations: ä = ae, ö = oe, ü = ue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method (historical and still common when typing is awkward) is widely understood by German speakers and acceptable when umlaut characters aren't available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronunciation practice resources (audio/video)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use linked audio recordings and a video to hear and visualize correct umlaut pronunciation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links short and long audio recordings for Ä, Ö, Ü and a video titled 'How to Pronounce an Umlaut | German Lessons' to aid practice and visualization.
